# TDPdf v2.0.1.0

**Electronic Signature now works inside TDPdf: you sign in with your browser instead of pasting a key, and signing pages open in a TDPdf window.**

## Sign in with your browser

**File ▸ Electronic Signature ▸ Connect** now opens the TDPdf Signing sign-in page in your browser. Sign in (or create a free account), choose **Allow**, and TDPdf is connected. You no longer need to create an API token and paste it.

Pasting a token still works under **Advanced**, for signing services that don't offer sign-in.

## Sign inside TDPdf

Signing pages now open in a TDPdf window instead of your browser:

- **Sign This Document** opens the signing page in TDPdf.
- **Sign on this computer** (in Signature Requests) lets someone sign at your desk.
- When the document is signed, TDPdf offers **Download signed copy** and **Open it** in the same window.

The window only shows the signing service. Any other link opens in your browser.

This uses the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, which Windows 11 includes. If it's missing, pages open in your browser as before and the status bar tells you how to get it.

## Signature Requests

- **Open** shows a request inside TDPdf.
- **Audit log & certificate** shows who did what and when.
- **Resend reminder** emails the people who still have to sign, and only those whose turn it is.

## Signed chip

A document's tab shows **Signed** when the file is the signed copy you downloaded from a completed request. It tells you where the file came from. It is not a signature check; use File ▸ Electronic Signature ▸ Verify Signatures for that.

## Privacy

The signing window keeps a small browser profile in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\TDPdf\WebView2`, so you stay signed in to the signing site. During sign-in, TDPdf listens on your own computer only (`127.0.0.1`) for up to five minutes. Both are described in the [privacy policy](https://tdpdf.com/privacy/).

## For IT

Nothing changes in how TDPdf installs. The admin guide ([docs/intune-distribution.md](https://github.com/doodlemania2/TDPdf/blob/main/docs/intune-distribution.md)) now covers the WebView2 Runtime, the sign-in listener, and the Electronic Signature policy keys.
